SourceString: Where faith meets power. Church officials shape morality, oversee tithes, and make sure laws keep one eye on heaven.
Political positions within the town's civic structure, open to any {CHAR_CITVSWOR_C}citizen{##} who meet the requirements and secure a fair victory in an {O_ELE_C}election{##}.
Consist of the {O_CHA_STAAUT_C}State Authority{##}, occupying ranks {icon_07} to {icon_09}.\nThey stand at the highest level of the town's political structure.
The city's whisper network. They gather secrets, expose rivals, and twist evidence into whatever story the council needs to hear. If something shady happens, they're the first to know.

Handle the lowest tiers of political authority, occupying ranks {icon_01} to {icon_03}.\nThey are {O_CHA_TOWSER_C}Town Servants{##}, {O_CHA_TOWBAI_C}Town Bailiffs{##}, and {O_CHA_INF_C}Informants{##}.
Operate within the central layers of political authority, occupying ranks {icon_04} to {icon_06}.\nThey are the {O_CHA_TOWCOU_C}Town Council{##} and {O_CHA_CHUAUT_C}Church Authority{##}.
The offices within this chamber are:
The bridge between city and realm. Senior councilors, commanders, and high clergy settle matters that stretch beyond town walls — levies, duties, and the wider balance of power.
The town's arm of law enforcement. Stationed at gates and walls, they enforce dues, guard against threats, and turn districts into safer ground under their watch.
The beating heart of town governance. Members debate laws, argue over money, and decide which improvements get built — or don't.
The first rung of city politics. Servants push papers, carry messages, and learn the ropes of administration. Everyone starts here — nobody stays here.
{L_LAW_C}Unlawful{##} acts that can leave {CR_EVI_C}evidence{##}. Crimes differ in how easily they're {CR_NOI_C}concealed{##} and how {CR_SEV_C}severe{##} they are.

Every {CR_CRI_C}crime{##} leaves a trace. Whether you witnessed it, suffered from it, {A_SPY_C}spied{##} on it, bought the information, or merely heard a whisper — evidence finds its way through the town.

Someone might be holding {CR_EVI_C}evidence{##} of your crimes. Confess at the Church or Buy an Indulgence to clear your name. Once you've faced Trial, regardless of the verdict, that {CR_EVI_C}evidence{##} can no longer be used against you. And {CR_STALIM_C}time{##}, as always, erases all sins.
You can place a {B_IMP_SPY_C}spyglass{##} in your home to {A_SPYPER_C}spy{##} on others. If you believe such work is better left to professionals, visit the {B_OCC_THI_C}Hideout{##} and hire one.
Use a {B_IMP_SPY_C}spyglass{##} in your home to {A_SPYPER_C}spy{##} on others, or hire a professional at the {B_OCC_THI_C}Hideout{##}.

When you hold {CR_EVI_C}evidence{##} of a crime, a righteous citizen would take it to the {B_PUB_TOWHAL_E}Town Hall{##} and {A_PRECHA_C}press charges{##}. Others may find more interesting uses for it.
With {CR_EVI_C}evidence{##} of a crime, you can {A_PRECHA_C}press charges{##} at the {B_PUB_TOWHAL_E}Town Hall{##}.
The harder a crime is to hide, the more {CR_EVI_C}evidence{##} it leaves — and the sooner trouble follows.
Reflects the gravity of each offense, classifying {CR_CRI_C}crimes{##} into five distinct levels. The higher the level, the harsher the {CR_TRIPUN_C}punishment{##}.
From most severe to least severe:
If caught, extreme crimes receive a {CR_TRIPUN_EXT_C}capital sentence{##}.
If caught, severe crimes receive a {CR_TRIPUN_MAJ_C}severe sentence{##}.
If caught, minor crimes receive a {CR_TRIPUN_MIN_C}minor sentence{##}.
If caught, major crimes receive a {CR_TRIPUN_SEV_C}major sentence{##}.
If caught, trivial crimes receive a {CR_TRIPUN_TRI_C}trivial sentence{##}.

Justice has an expiration date. Once a {CR_CRI_C}crime{##} is committed, a countdown begins. When the statute of limitations expires, any related {CR_EVI_C}evidence{##} is lost and can no longer be used.
This action is a crime of {crimeseverity} severity.
It is {CR_NOI_C}conspicuous{##} and likely to draw attention.
It is {CR_NOI_C}subtle{##} and not easily detected.
It is {CR_NOI_C}overt{##} and almost impossible to conceal.
When all appointing positions are vacant, the candidate is chosen by random draw.
Voting begins next turn at {hour}. Results will follow immediately after.

{CR_EVI_C}Evidence{##} has five degrees of strength.

The higher the degree, the stronger the proof — and the greater the chance of conviction. 

Gathering multiple pieces of evidence for the same crime increases the overall strength: two pieces of degree 1 combine into degree 2, and so on, up to a maximum of degree 5.
Always awarded to the most successful member of a guild or community. Unlike Civic Offices, these seats come from nomination rather than votes, and carry prestige without hierarchy.
Master of the Stone Masons' Guild
Public displays of poverty are considered distasteful. This law regulates begging, determining whether it's permitted or should remain out of sight.
Determines whether blackmail is a convenient diplomatic tool or just another crime to be punished.
Books and lampoons can propagate radical ideas (such as fair governance), giving the authorities the right to forbid their use.
A common method for securing the favor of those who could send you to prison, or smooth your way to the highest offices.
Regulates the construction fees in the city, impacting building costs.
Determines what percentage every believer must pay the Church as a tithe.
The rules that keep order in the city. Laws are set and shaped by those holding {O_TYP_CIVOFF_C}Civic Offices{##}, defining what is permitted — and what is not.
Decides whether duellists will be punished for their deed, provided that is still necessary…
Imposes a tax on guilds, contributing to the town's revenue.
The import duty protects the local commerce from outside competition, with revenue going to the town treasury.
Sets the salaries of all public officials. A convenient combination of civic duty and personal interest.
Oh, double misfortune! First, a loss in the family, then a fortune in taxes — at least the town treasury is richer.
\"If intelligence were an art, you'd be an empty canvas\". Whether such speech should be punishable is ruled by this law.
This law regulates whether it should be customary and permitted to demand a bit of ransom now and then when one happens to be “short of funds”… A curious law.
Sets the starting bid for securing leases on Resource Sites.
Determines whether practicing certain professions requires compulsory guild membership.
Regulates the practice of necromancy, including the raising of the dead or communicating with spirits.
Determines if helping yourself to someone else's coin purse deserves punishment.
Breaking this law may result in a {CR_TRIPUN_EXT_C}capital sentence{##}.
Breaking this law may result in a {CR_TRIPUN_MAJ_C}severe sentence{##}.
Breaking this law may result in a {CR_TRIPUN_MIN_C}minor sentence{##}.
Breaking this law may result in a {CR_TRIPUN_SEV_C}major sentence{##}.
Breaking this law may result in a {CR_TRIPUN_TRI_C}trivial sentence{##}.
Sets rent prices for workers in town, potentially influencing homelessness.
Regulates whether it's acceptable to secretly destroy property.
Every merchant must contribute to the greater good by handing over a portion of their sales earnings to those who contribute nothing at all.
Some rulers believe in second chances, others in iron-fisted justice. \nThe higher this law is, the harsher the {CR_TRIPUN_C}sentences{##}.
Defines whether breaking into properties and stealing from them is punishable by law.
This law traces the fine line between persuasion and harassment.
Pain can be an excellent teacher. This law determines whether Torture may be used as a means of interrogation and punishment.
Faith is a virtue, provided it is the correct one. Those found deviating from the accepted doctrine may find their faith tested under less-than-ideal conditions.
Determines whether hiring thugs in secrecy to beat someone up is legal.
This law determines whether or not people may fire off their cannon over the town with impunity.
Perfumes, often associated with vanity and moral decay, may be banned for personal use.
Is it science or sorcery? This law decides which one.
This law sets reasonable limits on loan rates, ensuring that lenders still make a fortune — just a slightly more respectable one.
Decides if it's perfectly fine to ambush a cart and make a quick profit.
Regulates the practice of witchcraft, including curses and the use of mystical objects.
Here you'll find the {L_LAW_C}laws{##} that hold the city together — and the {O_TYP_CIVOFF_C}offices{##} that enforce them.
Win an {O_ELE_C}election{##} to one of these roles, and you'll earn the power to shape those laws yourself.
{O_TYP_CIVOFF_C}Political authority{##} is divided among six chambers, each hierarchically organized with its own powers and duties.

{CHAR_CITVSWOR_C}Citizens{##} who meet the requirements may apply for {O_TYP_CIVOFF_C}office{##} in elections held the following {C_TRN_C}turn{##}. The appointers' good {CHAR_STA_C}opinion{##} of you — as well as strong {S_RHE_C}rhetoric{##} — can make all the difference.

Office progression is organized into ranks from {icon_01} to {icon_09}. 

If you wish to take part in the political life of the town, you must first become a citizen. 

From there, you begin at rank {icon_01} and work your way upward, step by step.

When you hold {CR_EVI_C}evidence{##} of a {CR_CRI_C}crime{##}, you may legally {A_PRECHA_C}press charges{##}. The {CR_TRI_JUR_C}Jury{##} decides whether the accused is guilty and should be {CR_TRIPUN_C}punished{##}, or absolved. If they are absolved, you must cover the costs of the proceedings, so try to be {S_RHE_C}convincing{##}.

However, if you are the one accused of a crime, do not rely on {S_RHE_C}rhetoric{##} alone. Try to {CHAR_STA_C}win over{##} the jury before the trial even begins. Perhaps {A_BRI_C}greasing their palms{##} would help — if that is not illegal, of course.

After being found guilty in a {CR_TRI_C}trial{##}, the accused is punished accordingly. The penalty depends on the {CR_SEV_C}severity of the crime{##} and how {L_LAWSEV_C}harsh{##} the current law is.
If the accused is absolved, the crime is erased from their record, and the accuser must pay for the trial proceedings.

To deliver a fair verdict in a {CR_TRI_C}trial{##}, the jury evaluates the {CR_EVI_C}evidence{##} and {S_RHE_C}arguments{##} from both sides.\nStill, partiality and {CHAR_STA_C}opinion{##} may sway their judgment.
In case of a tie, position {icon_01} has the deciding vote. If vacant, position {icon_02} decides. If all members are absent, the accused is {CR_TRIPUN_C}absolved{##}.
If any of these positions are vacant, a substitute juror will be assigned.
By decision of the jury, {gender}|gender({charactername} is guilty, {charactername} is guilty).
By decision of the jury, {gender}|gender({charactername} is absolved, {charactername} is absolved).
By applying for this position, you give up your right to vote in this election.
You cannot be both an appointer and a candidate in the same election. You can no longer vote.
As both an appointer and a candidate, your vote is automatically cast for yourself.
